{\sffamily\small\color{inkgrey} Start with \code{import simplydata as sdata}. A command that begins with
\code{table.} works on a table from \code{sdata.table(...)}; \code{chart.} on a chart from
\code{table.start\_chart()} or \code{sdata.chart(...)}; \code{nums.} on numbers from \code{sdata.numbers(...)}.
The small grey line under a command names its options. For the full story of a command, use
\code{sdata.help("word")}, the \href{https://github.com/bioforkgithub/simplydata/blob/main/docs/manual/simplydata_manual.pdf}{manual} or the \href{https://github.com/bioforkgithub/simplydata/blob/main/docs/manual/simplydataDictionary.pdf}{dictionary}. These cards are
made from simplydata's own code by \code{docs/make\_cheat\_sheet.py}, so they always match the version above.\par}

\card{Start, show and save}{1}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}chart(sdata.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}example(\textquotedbl{}marks\textquotedbl{}))}\opts{\code{data=}, \code{sheet=}, \code{fast=}}}{Start a chart.}{seaborn \code{scatterplot()}}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}example(\textquotedbl{}marks\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{name=}, \code{from\_\allowbreak{}r\_\allowbreak{}package=}}}{A small table to practise with.}{pandas \code{files()}}

\cmd{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}show()}}{Show the chart in a window.}{matplotlib \code{barplot()}, \code{show()}}

\cmd{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}save(\textquotedbl{}marks.\allowbreak{}png\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{file\_\allowbreak{}name}, \code{quality=}, \code{resolution=}, \code{dpi=}}}{Save the chart.}{matplotlib \code{barplot()}, \code{savefig()}, \code{path.\allowbreak{}join()}, \code{gettempdir()}}

\cmd{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}numbers\_\allowbreak{}drawn()}}{A table of the numbers the chart drew.}{matplotlib \code{scatter()}, \code{collections.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}offsets()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

Every pair is compared, with Holm's correction.}{SciPy (stats.ttest\_ind or mannwhitneyu, \code{tukey\_\allowbreak{}hsd}, dunnett), with Holm's correction from statsmodels (multipletests); R wilcox.test for exact Mann-Whitney p-values with tied values; R rstatix::\code{games\_\allowbreak{}howell\_\allowbreak{}test}, DescTools::ScheffeTest and PostHocTest, FSA::dunnTest, PMCMRplus::kwAllPairsConoverTest and multcompView::multcompLetters for \code{show=\textquotedbl{}letters\textquotedbl{}} (simplydata[r]); SciPy \code{ttest\_\allowbreak{}rel} and wilcoxon for \code{matched\_\allowbreak{}by=}, R PMCMRplus::frdAllPairsNemenyiTest and frdAllPairsConoverTest after Friedman (\code{test\_\allowbreak{}method=}); SciPy \code{chi2\_\allowbreak{}contingency} or \code{fisher\_\allowbreak{}exact}, statsmodels \code{confint\_\allowbreak{}proportions\_\allowbreak{}2indep} for \code{based\_\allowbreak{}on=\textquotedbl{}percents\textquotedbl{}}}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}compare\_\allowbreak{}risks(\textquotedbl{}died\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} for\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}group\_\allowbreak{}in=\textquotedbl{}treatment\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} against=\textquotedbl{}usual care\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{column=}, \code{for\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}group\_\allowbreak{}in=}, \code{against=}, \code{value=}, \code{allowing\_\allowbreak{}for=}, \code{interval=}, \code{p\_\allowbreak{}value\_\allowbreak{}by=}, \code{same\_\allowbreak{}within=}, \code{not\_\allowbreak{}lower=}, \code{not\_\allowbreak{}higher=} and 5 more}}{How much more (or less) often does something happen in one group than in another?}{statsmodels (\code{proportion\_\allowbreak{}confint}, \code{confint\_\allowbreak{}proportions\_\allowbreak{}2indep} with Newcombe's interval, Table2x2, StratifiedTable for \code{allowing\_\allowbreak{}for=}, \code{tost\_\allowbreak{}proportions\_\allowbreak{}2indep} for \code{same\_\allowbreak{}within=}); SciPy (\code{chi2\_\allowbreak{}contingency}, \code{fisher\_\allowbreak{}exact}, contingency.odds\_ratio); R epiR::epi.2by2 for the interval of the Mantel-Haenszel risk ratio and prop.test for one-sided p-values, and epiR::epi.2by2 for \code{show=\textquotedbl{}attributable fractions\textquotedbl{}} (simplydata[r])}

\card{Undo and finish}{39}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}undo()}}{Take the last step back.}{simplydata's own: it keeps the table as it was before each step and puts back the last one. In pandas or Polars you keep a copy yourself before a step (before = \code{df.\allowbreak{}copy()}) and go back to it.}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}steps()}}{List every step you did to this table, in order.}{simplydata's own: it writes down each step as you do it and lists them. pandas and Polars keep no list of steps; your script is the record.}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}again()}}{Go back to the table as it was at the start.}{simplydata's own: it keeps the table it started with and puts it back, as one more step that \code{undo()} can take back. In pandas or Polars you keep the first table yourself (start = \code{df.\allowbreak{}copy()}) and go back to it.}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}save(\textquotedbl{}clean.\allowbreak{}xlsx\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{file\_\allowbreak{}name}, \code{in\_\allowbreak{}sheet=}}}{Save the table; the end of the file name decides the type.}{pandas \code{TemporaryDirectory()}, \code{to\_\allowbreak{}csv()}, \code{path.\allowbreak{}join()} \textperiodcentered{} Polars \code{TemporaryDirectory()}, \code{write\_\allowbreak{}csv()}, \code{path.\allowbreak{}join()}}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}copy()}}{Give back an independent copy of the table.}{pandas \code{copy()}, \code{boolean indexing} \textperiodcentered{} Polars \code{clone()}, \code{filter()}, \code{col()}}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}chart()}}{Start a chart from this table.}{seaborn \code{boolean indexing}, \code{barplot()}}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}as\_\allowbreak{}pandas()}}{Give back the table as a plain pandas table, for other Python tools.}{Polars \code{to\_\allowbreak{}pandas()}}

\cmd{\code{table.\allowbreak{}as\_\allowbreak{}polars()}}{Give back the table as a plain Polars table, for other Python tools.}{pandas \code{read\_\allowbreak{}csv()}, \code{from\_\allowbreak{}pandas()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}column(1)}\opts{\code{position=}}}{One column of the grid as new numbers, counting from 1: \code{get\_\allowbreak{}column(1)} is the left one.}{NumPy \code{copy()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}all\_\allowbreak{}numbers()}}{All the numbers of the grid as a list, row by row (flatten).}{NumPy \code{ravel().\allowbreak{}copy()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}keep\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position(1,\allowbreak{} to=2)}\opts{\code{positions=}, \code{to=}, \code{step=}}}{Keep rows of the grid by their position, counting from 1: a run, every n-th row, or a list.}{NumPy \code{arange().\allowbreak{}reshape()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}keep\_\allowbreak{}columns\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position(2,\allowbreak{} to=3)}\opts{\code{positions=}, \code{to=}, \code{step=}}}{Keep columns of the grid by their position, counting from 1 at the left.}{NumPy \code{arange().\allowbreak{}reshape()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}remove\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position(1)}\opts{\code{positions=}, \code{to=}, \code{step=}}}{Remove rows of the grid by their position, counting from 1.}{NumPy \code{arange().\allowbreak{}reshape()}, \code{delete()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}remove\_\allowbreak{}columns\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position(1)}\opts{\code{positions=}, \code{to=}, \code{step=}}}{Remove columns of the grid by their position, counting from 1 at the left.}{NumPy \code{arange().\allowbreak{}reshape()}, \code{delete()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}replace\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}that(is\_\allowbreak{}below=4,\allowbreak{} with\_\allowbreak{}value=0)}\opts{\code{old=}, \code{with\_\allowbreak{}value=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}above=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}below=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}least=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}most=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}equal\_\allowbreak{}to=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}not\_\allowbreak{}equal\_\allowbreak{}to=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}between=}, \code{is\_\allowbreak{}one\_\allowbreak{}of=} and 1 more}}{Replace a number, or every number that meets one condition; the grid keeps its rows and columns.}{NumPy \code{where()}}

\cmd{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}swap\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}and\_\allowbreak{}columns()}}{Turn rows into columns and columns into rows (the transpose in maths).}{NumPy \code{T.\allowbreak{}copy()}}

\end{cardtable}

\card{Numbers: undo and finish}{45}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}undo()}}{Take the last step back.}{simplydata's own: it keeps the numbers as they were before each step (up to 30 steps) and puts back the last one. With NumPy you keep a copy yourself before a step (before = \code{values.\allowbreak{}copy()}).}

\cmd{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}steps()}}{List every step you did, in order.}{simplydata's own: it writes down each step as you do it and lists them. A NumPy array keeps no list of steps; your script is the record.}

\cmd{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}again()}}{Go back to the numbers as they were at the start.}{simplydata's own: it keeps the numbers you started with and puts them back, as one more step that \code{undo()} can take back. With NumPy you keep the first array yourself.}

\cmd{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}turn\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}table(name=\textquotedbl{}marks\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{name=}}}{Turn the numbers into a simplydata table.}{pandas \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}chart()}}{Start a chart from these numbers.}{seaborn \code{DataFrame()}, \code{histplot()}}

\cmd{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}save(\textquotedbl{}nums.\allowbreak{}csv\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{file\_\allowbreak{}name}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}step=}, \code{bits=}}}{Save the numbers; the end of the file name decides the type.}{pandas \code{TemporaryDirectory()}, \code{DataFrame().\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}csv()}, \code{path.\allowbreak{}join()}}

\cmd{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}as\_\allowbreak{}numpy()}}{Give back the numbers as a plain NumPy array, for other Python tools.}{NumPy \code{copy()}}

\end{cardtable}

\card{Waves and systems}{46}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}convolve\_\allowbreak{}with([1,\allowbreak{} 2,\allowbreak{} 1])}\opts{\code{other}, \code{keep=}}}{Convolve the numbers with other numbers: each result is a sum of products as one list slides along.}{SciPy \code{convolve()}}

\cmd{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}deconvolve\_\allowbreak{}by([1,\allowbreak{} 2,\allowbreak{} 3])}\opts{\code{other}}}{Undo a convolution: the numbers divided by other numbers (polynomial division).}{SciPy \code{deconvolve()}}

\cmd{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}change\_\allowbreak{}time\_\allowbreak{}step(to=0.\allowbreak{}01,\allowbreak{} time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}001)}\opts{\code{to=}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}step=}, \code{test\_\allowbreak{}method=}, \code{sampling\_\allowbreak{}rate=}, \code{fs=}}}{Change the time between readings (resample): fewer readings (with a filter first) or more.}{SciPy \code{round()}, \code{resample()}}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}wave(\textquotedbl{}sine\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} frequency=5,\allowbreak{} time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}01,\allowbreak{} how\_\allowbreak{}many=100)}\opts{\code{shape=}, \code{frequency=}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}step=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{high\_\allowbreak{}share=}, \code{rising\_\allowbreak{}share=}, \code{sweep=}, \code{bandwidth=}, \code{at=}, \code{sampling\_\allowbreak{}rate=} and 1 more}}{Numbers that make a wave: a sine, square, sawtooth, chirp, pulse or impulse.}{SciPy \code{arange()}, \code{square()}}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}window\_\allowbreak{}shape(\textquotedbl{}hann\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} how\_\allowbreak{}many=64)}\opts{\code{name=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{periodic=}}}{The weights of a window (taper), such as \code{\textquotedbl{}hann\textquotedbl{}}: high in the middle, low at the ends.}{SciPy \code{get\_\allowbreak{}window()}}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}system(\textquotedbl{}1 / (s**2 + 2*s + 5)\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{formula=}, \code{numerator=}, \code{denominator=}, \code{poles=}, \code{zeros=}, \code{gain=}, \code{a=}, \code{b=}, \code{c=}, \code{d=} and 7 more}}{A linear system (one input, one output) from its formula, coefficients, poles or matrices.}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}step\_\allowbreak{}response(until=10)}\opts{\code{until=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}points=}}}{How the output answers an input that jumps from 0 to 1 and stays there.}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{step()}, \code{linspace()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}impulse\_\allowbreak{}response(until=10)}\opts{\code{until=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}points=}}}{How the output answers a short kick at time 0 (an impulse of size 1).}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{impulse()}, \code{linspace()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}response\_\allowbreak{}to(sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}wave(\textquotedbl{}square\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} frequency=0.\allowbreak{}2,\allowbreak{} time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}05,\allowbreak{} how\_\allowbreak{}many=400))}\opts{\code{inputs=}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}points=}}}{How the output answers any input you give: a simulation.}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{arange()}, \code{square()}, \code{lsim()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}frequency\_\allowbreak{}response(between=[0.\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{} 100])}\opts{\code{between=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{unit=}}}{How much the system passes each frequency (gain) and how much it delays it (phase): the Bode data.}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{freqresp()}, \code{logspace()}, \code{DataFrame()}, \code{abs()}, \code{log10()}, \code{degrees()}, \code{unwrap()}, \code{angle()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}poles()}}{The poles: the values of s (or z) where the bottom of the formula is 0. They set how it moves.}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{DataFrame()}, \code{abs()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}zeros()}}{The zeros: the values of s (or z) where the top of the formula is 0 (inputs that do not get through).}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{DataFrame()}, \code{abs()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}is\_\allowbreak{}stable()}}{True when every response to a bounded input stays bounded (and settles).}{SciPy \code{bool()}, \code{all()}, \code{lti()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}steady\_\allowbreak{}gain()}}{Where the output settles for a constant input of 1 (the DC gain).}{NumPy \code{polyval()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}in\_\allowbreak{}steps(time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}1)}\opts{\code{time\_\allowbreak{}step=}, \code{test\_\allowbreak{}method=}}}{The same system in steps of \code{time\_\allowbreak{}step} (discrete time), for a computer that reads and acts in steps.}{SciPy \code{cont2discrete()}, \code{DataFrame()}, \code{ravel()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}then(sdata.\allowbreak{}system(\textquotedbl{}1 / s\textquotedbl{}))}\opts{\code{other}}}{This system, then another one after it (in series): the output of this one feeds the other.}{NumPy \code{polymul()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}add(sdata.\allowbreak{}system(\textquotedbl{}1 / (s + 3)\textquotedbl{}))}\opts{\code{other}}}{This system and another side by side, their outputs added (in parallel): both get the same input.}{NumPy \code{polyadd()}, \code{polymul()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}with\_\allowbreak{}feedback()}\opts{\code{through=}, \code{sign=}}}{The closed loop: the output is fed back (through a sensor, say) and taken from the input.}{NumPy \code{polymul()}, \code{polyadd()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}table()}\opts{\code{form=}}}{The system as numbers: \code{form=\textquotedbl{}transfer function\textquotedbl{}} (the coefficients of the top and the bottom, highest power first: power of s (power of z in steps), numerator, denominator), \code{\textquotedbl{}state space\textquotedbl{}} (the matrices A, B, C, D in controller form: matrix, row, column, value; SciPy tf2ss, as R control::tf2ss) or \code{\textquotedbl{}poles and zeros\textquotedbl{}} (kind, real part, imaginary part; the last row is the gain).}{SciPy \code{lti()}, \code{concatenate()}, \code{zeros()}, \code{DataFrame()}}

\cmd{\code{system.\allowbreak{}chart()}\opts{\code{show=}, \code{between=}, \code{until=}, \code{unit=}}}{A chart of the system: \code{show=\textquotedbl{}bode\textquotedbl{}} (gain in decibels and phase against frequency on a log scale, two panels; \code{\textquotedbl{}gain and phase\textquotedbl{}} is accepted), \code{\textquotedbl{}step\textquotedbl{}}, \code{\textquotedbl{}impulse\textquotedbl{}}, \code{\textquotedbl{}poles and zeros\textquotedbl{}} (x for poles, o for zeros; the unit circle for a system in steps; \code{\textquotedbl{}pole-zero\textquotedbl{}} is accepted) or \code{\textquotedbl{}nyquist\textquotedbl{}} (the frequency response as one curve; a feedback loop is stable when it stays clear of -1).}{matplotlib \code{lti()}, \code{freqresp()}, \code{findfreqs()}, \code{plot()}, \code{log10()}, \code{abs()}, \code{set\_\allowbreak{}ylabel()}, \code{degrees()}, \code{unwrap()}, \code{angle()}, \code{set\_\allowbreak{}xscale()}, \code{set\_\allowbreak{}xlabel()}}

\end{cardtable}

\card{Help}{47}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}all\_\allowbreak{}words()}}{Print every simplydata word with a short example.}{simplydata's own: it prints its own word list, group by group, with a short example of each.}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}help(\textquotedbl{}draw\_\allowbreak{}bars\textquotedbl{})}\opts{\code{word=}}}{Explain one word: what it does, its options and an example you can run.}{simplydata's own: it reads its own word list and the words' docstrings, in plain Python. Python's \code{help()} shows a function's docstring too.}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}lesson(1)}\opts{\code{number=}, \code{solutions=}}}{A lesson: an example to run, what each line does, and a task.}{simplydata's own: the lessons are written in simplydata (learn.py) and printed in plain Python; nothing is computed.}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}packages\_\allowbreak{}used()}\opts{\code{save\_\allowbreak{}as=}, \code{at\_\allowbreak{}end=}}}{List the packages that did the work behind your simplydata words, and how to cite them.}{simplydata's own: it notes which packages its words called, reads their versions from the installed metadata (Python's importlib.metadata; R's \code{packageVersion()} and \code{citation()} through rpy2 for R packages) and prints each reference with a sentence for your methods. No data are worked on; \code{importlib.\allowbreak{}metadata.\allowbreak{}version(\textquotedbl{}pandas\textquotedbl{})} gives one version yourself.}

\end{cardtable}

\card{30 days of simplydata}{48}

\begin{cardtable}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}30\_\allowbreak{}days()}\opts{\code{track=}, \code{start\_\allowbreak{}again=}}}{Start 30 days of simplydata: an hour a day of warm-up questions, lessons and tasks.}{simplydata's own: the 30 days are written in simplydata (\code{learn\_\allowbreak{}days}.py) and printed in plain Python; the day you reached is kept in a small JSON file on this computer (json, pathlib), and nothing is computed or sent anywhere.}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}today()}\opts{\code{follow\_\allowbreak{}calendar=}}}{Show today's day of the 30 days of simplydata: warm-up questions, what to do and a task.}{simplydata's own: the 30 days are written in simplydata (\code{learn\_\allowbreak{}days}.py) and printed in plain Python; the day you reached is kept in a small JSON file on this computer (json, pathlib), and nothing is computed or sent anywhere.}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}day(5)}\opts{\code{number=}, \code{track=}}}{Show any day of the 30 days, without changing where you are.}{simplydata's own: the 30 days are written in simplydata (\code{learn\_\allowbreak{}days}.py) and printed in plain Python; nothing is computed.}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}answers(5)}\opts{\code{number=}, \code{track=}}}{The answers to a day's warm-up questions, and a worked answer to its task.}{simplydata's own: the answers are written in simplydata (\code{learn\_\allowbreak{}days}.py) and printed in plain Python; nothing is computed.}

\cmd{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}go\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}next\_\allowbreak{}day()}}{Go on to the next day now, without waiting for tomorrow.}{simplydata's own: the 30 days are written in simplydata (\code{learn\_\allowbreak{}days}.py) and printed in plain Python; the day you reached is kept in a small JSON file on this computer (json, pathlib), and nothing is computed or sent anywhere.}

\end{cardtable}
